findings.title: Index is created without CONCURRENTLY on a ~400M-row table
findings.explanation: A plain CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock on `events`. That lock blocks all INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the table for the whole build, which on 400M rows could take many minutes. Event writes would stall or time out, and this would be a production outage during deploy. docs/CONVENTIONS.md requires `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` for this table, and migration 004 already does this. Change the statement to `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);`.

findings.title: Missing `-- migrate:no-transaction` header
findings.explanation: CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block. The migration runner wraps files in a transaction by default, so the fixed statement would fail without the header. Add `-- migrate:no-transaction` as the first line, as 004_events.sql does.

findings.title: Use IF NOT EXISTS and handle failed concurrent builds
findings.explanation: A failed CONCURRENTLY build leaves an INVALID index behind. Re-running the migration then fails because the name already exists. Consider `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS`, and document that an invalid index must be dropped with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY` before retrying. Without this, a retry after a failure needs manual cleanup. Also check statement_timeout and lock_timeout for the migration role, so the long build is not cancelled.
